title: Dual inhibition of EGR1/STAT3 transcriptional hubs suppresses macrophage-driven liver fibrosis: A multi-omics-guided drug repurposing strategy.
authors: Mijit, Arzu; Zhang, Yong-Zheng; Wu, Yang; Li, Mengjia; Wang, Zihang; Cheng, Lu-Feng
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过多组学与CADD/MD模拟筛选靶向EGR1/STAT3转录因子的药物，虽涉及TF-DNA结合域抑制，但核心是药物重定位与肝纤维化治疗，而非TF-DNA互作机制建模。
abstract: Liver fibrosis (LF), driven by dysregulated macrophage polarization and extracellular matrix remodeling, represents a critical and unmet therapeutic challenge in chronic liver diseases. Despite decades of research, the lack of agents targeting core transcriptional regulators of fibrogenesis underscores the urgent need for mechanism-based interventions. An integrative analysis of three single-cell transcriptomic atlases identified Early Growth Response 1 (EGR1) and Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 3 (STAT3) as central transcriptional regulators that orchestrate pro-fibrotic macrophage polarization and the downstream activation of fibrogenic effectors such as Arginase 1 (Arg1), Fibronectin 1 (Fn1), Osteopontin (Spp1), and Thrombospondin 1 (Thbs1). By leveraging computer-aided drug design (CADD), multi-precision virtual screening of both the FDA-approved drug library and the TCMSP drug database identified Cidofovir and Pioglitazone as novel inhibitors selectively targeting EGR1 and STAT3, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable binding interactions at their DNA-binding domains. Functional validation in macrophages showed that Cidofovir suppressed EGR1 signaling and downstream fibrotic gene expression, while Pioglitazone inhibited STAT3 activity and M2 macrophage polarization. In a murine LF model, dual therapy synergistically reduced collagen deposition and hepatic stellate cell activation, exhibiting superior efficacy compared to monotherapy. This study pioneers the therapeutic repositioning of Cidofovir and Pioglitazone as dual-target transcriptional inhibitors, disrupting the EGR1/STAT3-Fn1/Spp1/Thbs1 axis to attenuate fibrotic niche formation. Our "multi-omics to bedside" framework, empowered by computer-aided drug design, not only deciphers macrophage-centric fibrogenic networks but also delivers clinically translatable candidates, bridging the gap between computational drug discovery and precision antifibrotic therapy.
abstract_zh: 肝纤维化（LF）由失调的巨噬细胞极化和细胞外基质重塑驱动，是慢性肝病中一个关键且尚未满足的治疗挑战。尽管经过数十年的研究，缺乏靶向纤维发生核心转录调控因子的药物，凸显了对基于机制的干预措施的迫切需求。对三个单细胞转录组图谱的综合分析，鉴定出早期生长反应因子1（EGR1）和信号转导与转录激活因子3（STAT3）为核心转录调控因子，它们协调促纤维化巨噬细胞极化及下游纤维化效应因子（如精氨酸酶1（Arg1）、纤连蛋白1（Fn1）、骨桥蛋白（Spp1）和血小板反应蛋白1（Thbs1））的激活。通过利用计算机辅助药物设计（CADD），对FDA批准药物库和TCMSP药物数据库进行多精度虚拟筛选，鉴定出西多福韦和吡格列酮分别作为选择性靶向EGR1和STAT3的新型抑制剂。分子动力学模拟确认了它们在其DNA结合域上的稳定结合相互作用。巨噬细胞中的功能验证表明，西多福韦抑制EGR1信号传导及下游纤维化基因表达，而吡格列酮抑制STAT3活性和M2巨噬细胞极化。在小鼠LF模型中，双药联合治疗协同减少胶原沉积和肝星状细胞活化，与单药治疗相比表现出更优疗效。本研究开创了西多福韦和吡格列酮作为双靶点转录抑制剂治疗性重定位的先河，通过破坏EGR1/STAT3-Fn1/Spp1/Thbs1轴来减轻纤维化微环境形成。我们的“多组学到临床”框架，借助计算机辅助药物设计，不仅解析了以巨噬细胞为中心的纤维化网络，还提供了临床可转化的候选药物，弥合了计算药物发现与精准抗纤维化治疗之间的鸿沟。
